_ai_assisted: AI-assisted: protocol structure regenerated with Codex under Edu decisions for #137, then reviewed and rewritten with Claude against guia_tratamientos_vigilancia_urgencia.pdf; human review by Edu pending.
_integration_status: Activated for confirmed numerical findings. Immediate clinical-priority entry before measurement confirmation remains a separate owner integration; no numerical finding automatically establishes urgency.

route.source: Prototype flow composition [P]: no published primary source.

w_red_flags.text: Are any of these present: sudden or rapidly worsening weakness, new inability to move safely or complete egress, new intense muscle pain, breathing difficulty, or loss of consciousness? Breathing difficulty or unconsciousness is a general emergency, not proof of atrophy.
w_red_flags.source: Urgency symptom list: Team triage proposal [P]: no published primary source.

w_escalate.source: Team triage proposal [P]: no published primary source.

w_concern.source: NASA OCHMO-TB-031, Exercise Overview [1] (https://www.nasa.gov/ochmo-tb-031-exercise-overview-2/): in-mission strength standard of at least 80 % of baseline. Priority review of a concern-level finding: Team triage proposal [P]: no published primary source.

w_limits.text: Is the worsening unexpected, or does it stop you from completing a task?
w_limits.source: Priority assessment for unexpected worsening or task limitation: Team triage proposal [P]: no published primary source.

w_priority_review.text: Ask the crew medical officer for priority assessment of your capacity and of the cause of the concerning finding or unexpected task limitation. A concerning number alone does not establish a medical urgency.
w_priority_review.source: NASA OCHMO-TB-031, Exercise Overview [1] (https://www.nasa.gov/ochmo-tb-031-exercise-overview-2/): in-mission strength standard of at least 80 % of baseline. Priority assessment: Team triage proposal [P]: no published primary source.

w_review_outcome.text: Answer once the clinician has completed the priority assessment; until then stay on this step. Has the clinician declared a medical urgency?
w_review_outcome.source: Clinician-held escalation after a priority review: Team triage proposal [P]: no published primary source.

w_report.text: Tell the crew medical officer. Review together your symptoms, any pain, your real exercise load and your strength trend; these symptoms are nonspecific, so other causes are checked too.
w_report.source: NASA OCHMO-TB-031, Exercise Overview [1] (https://www.nasa.gov/ochmo-tb-031-exercise-overview-2/): specialists monitor crew fitness and exercise performed in flight. NASA, The Real Story About Astronaut Health Care in Space [3] (https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/faq-the-real-story-about-astronaut-health-care-in-space/): regular contact with doctors. Notification step: Team triage proposal [P]: no published primary source.

w_exercise.text: Review resistive and aerobic load, technique and recovery with your exercise specialist rather than increasing load yourself. Correct any energy deficit and review protein intake against the approved nutrition plan.
w_exercise.source: NASA OCHMO-TB-031, Exercise Overview [1] (https://www.nasa.gov/ochmo-tb-031-exercise-overview-2/): individual prescriptions by exercise specialists. NASA, Human Adaptation to Spaceflight: The Role of Nutrition [2] (https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/human-adaptation-to-spaceflight-the-role-of-nutrition.pdf): adequate energy and protein first, protein supplements not required.

w_end.text: Log symptoms and training daily; repeat comparable strength tests as directed and follow prescribed rehabilitation after return. Do not train through pain, add catch-up overload, or start supplements or medicines without medical advice.
w_end.source: NASA, The Real Story About Astronaut Health Care in Space [3] (https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/faq-the-real-story-about-astronaut-health-care-in-space/) and NASA OCHMO-TB-031, Exercise Overview [1] (https://www.nasa.gov/ochmo-tb-031-exercise-overview-2/): progressive post-flight reconditioning. Canadian Space Agency, Return and Reconditioning [4] (https://www.asc-csa.gc.ca/eng/youth-educators/activities/fitness-and-nutrition/return-and-reconditioning.asp). Daily log and avoid list: Team triage proposal [P]: no published primary source.

u_stop.text: Stop exercise and risky tasks, get to a safe position and alert the crew medical officer immediately. Do not repeat maximal tests, force yourself to walk or exercise, or wait for another sensor reading.
u_stop.source: Stop-exercise and no-maximal-test response: Team triage proposal [P]: no published primary source.

u_local.text: Activate the on-board medical lead to secure you and for immediate assessment and stabilization; sudden weakness is not assumed to be chronic atrophy, so injury or another acute illness is looked for. Follow the emergency protocol as trained, without waiting for Earth.
u_local.source: Immediate assessment and stabilization, looking for an acute cause: Team triage proposal [P]: no published primary source.

u_env.source: NASA, The Real Story About Astronaut Health Care in Space [3] (https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/faq-the-real-story-about-astronaut-health-care-in-space/): flight surgeons follow each crew during the mission. NASA, Hazard: Distance From Earth [7] (https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/hazard-distance-from-earth/): delayed Earth support at Mars. Routing by environment: Team triage proposal [P]: no published primary source.

u_moon.text: Care continues on board or in the habitat; this alert does not trigger an evacuation. The clinician evaluates any transfer according to vehicle and resources and decides whether to request Earth support.
u_moon.source: Moon routing (care on board, transfer evaluated by the clinician, no Earth contact named): Team triage proposal [P]: no published primary source.

u_earth.text: Send the case to the flight surgeons for remote medical support; this app does not send the message itself. Do not wait for the reply: on-board care continues under the local emergency protocol.
u_earth.source: NASA, The Real Story About Astronaut Health Care in Space [3] (https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/faq-the-real-story-about-astronaut-health-care-in-space/): flight surgeons follow each crew during the mission. NASA, Hazard: Distance From Earth [7] (https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/hazard-distance-from-earth/): up to 20 minutes one-way delay at Mars, crews act with minimal Earth support.

u_handover.text: Confirm that a clinician has reviewed this episode and accepted responsibility for ongoing care. Select Done only then; otherwise keep this task active and stay assisted.
u_handover.source: Urgency held until clinician acceptance; crew acknowledgement, not authenticated sign-off (Edu decision, #137): Team triage proposal [P]: no published primary source.

u_end.text: Accepted handover is recorded; EVA and demanding tasks stay suspended until the clinician decides. Rehabilitation follows the diagnosis, exertion resumes only when authorized, and any return or transfer depends on care capacity, vehicle and resources, not a sensor value.
u_end.source: NASA, The Real Story About Astronaut Health Care in Space [3] (https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/faq-the-real-story-about-astronaut-health-care-in-space/): return in the crew's spacecraft if an emergency requires it. NASA OCHMO-TB-031, Exercise Overview [1] (https://www.nasa.gov/ochmo-tb-031-exercise-overview-2/): post-flight reconditioning. Task suspension until clinical decision: Team triage proposal [P]: no published primary source.
